name: San Marino
headline: San Marino: +1.5% growth in 2025, 2.2% inflation, debt 60% of GDP
sections: San Marino is a $2.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 192nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.5% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $79K at purchasing-power parity (2023), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 31.8% of GDP (2023).
Consumer prices rose 2.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%.
Gross government debt is 60% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 70% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.6% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +17.1% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 341% of GDP (2023), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were −0.9% of GDP (2023).
IMF projections put government debt at 44% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 85.8 years (2024). Population: 34 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
